subject: Why isn't ggplot2 installed by default along with R?

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: Why isn't ggplot2 installed by default along with R?
parts:
On 11-10-21 08:40 PM, xuwang wrote:
> I searched but could not find any information on this. I'm guessing
> there must be a good reason. People must use ggplot2 more than some
> other things that come installed by default, for example Sweave. Or
> does ggplot2 take up a lot of space?
>
> I'm very curious.

There are a very small number of 'recommended' packages that are
installed by default with R. R-core (the core team of developers who
develop and maintain 'base R') are *extremely* conservative about adding
new packages to this list, and have even talked about trying to take
functionality *out* of base R. As long as packages are available via
CRAN, R-core doesn't see why they should take on the commitment to
maintain particular them.

I do feel that handling of the package ecosystem is one place where R
could use improvement (although it's not an easy problem -- Hadley has
tried by starting CRANtastic, but it hasn't really taken off)
